prompt_rules: Preserve Japanese script. Supply consistent Modified Hepburn romanization with macrons. Keep particles and auxiliaries aligned to the user's tokenization; do not claim that automatic word units settle morphological analysis.

Preserve German orthography, capitalization, compounds, and separable-verb word order. Do not invent segmentable affixes for fused exponents; use Leipzig periods for bundled features when appropriate.
Preserve French accents, apostrophes, hyphens, and surface contractions. A fused form such as aux may receive a bundled gloss such as to.ART.PL; do not fabricate hyphen boundaries.

Preserve Spanish accents and ñ. Treat al, del, and attached clitics conservatively; keep the surface token and use equals signs only when the analysis is justified. Do not add an unexpressed subject token.

Preserve Dutch orthographic tokens and separable-particle order. Do not split fixed contractions mechanically. Avoid COM for common gender because Leipzig COM means comitative; use an explicitly declared label such as COMMON.

Use scholarly IAST for Devanagari input. Preserve the surface form and user-supplied boundaries. Sandhi segmentation is analysis, not character transliteration; place uncertain alternatives in the note instead of silently rewriting the source.

Use modern reversible ULY/NUL: خ=x, چ=ch, ش=sh, ق=q, ك=k, غ=gh, ې=ë, ە=e, ۆ=ö, and ۈ=ü. Preserve logical token order. Never emit bidi override characters; Arabic form is RTL while romanization and glosses are LTR.

Keep Cyrillic and traditional Mongolian as distinct script profiles; they are not losslessly interchangeable. Preserve variation selectors and joiners in traditional-script forms and name the selected romanization scheme explicitly.

Use THL Extended Wylie for reversible orthographic transliteration. Preserve tsheg and stacked-letter sequences. A tsheg delimits a syllabic unit, not necessarily a linguistic word; respect the user's whitespace boundaries.
